cards.b: Nerves are fast text messages; hormones are letters sent by blood. They control growth, mood, sugar levels, puberty and stress. Diabetes, thyroid disease and growth disorders are hormone problems, and all are common in India.

Hormones are chemical messengers made by glands and carried in blood to target cells that have matching receptors. William Bayliss and Ernest Starling coined the word in 1905 after discovering secretin. Control is usually by negative feedback.

A pea-sized gland under the brain. It makes growth hormone (too little: dwarfism; too much: gigantism), TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, prolactin, and stores ADH and oxytocin from the hypothalamus. ADH helps the kidney save water.
The thyroid makes thyroxine, which sets metabolism and needs iodine. Lack of iodine causes goitre. Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium; calcitonin lowers it.

After a meal, the pancreas releases insulin, which makes cells absorb glucose and liver store glycogen. Between meals, glucagon releases glucose. In type 1 diabetes the body makes no insulin; in type 2 cells respond poorly. Banting and Best (1921, Toronto) isolated insulin; Banting and Macleod got the 1923 Nobel.

The adrenal medulla releases adrenaline in seconds: heart races, glucose rises. The cortex releases cortisol (long stress) and aldosterone (salt balance). Chronic stress keeps cortisol high and harms health.

Testes make testosterone; ovaries make oestrogen and progesterone. Melatonin from the pineal gland sets sleep rhythm. Plants also use hormones: auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, ethylene and abscisic acid.

Arnold Berthold (1849) moved a rooster's testes and found comb and behaviour preserved, hinting at chemical signals. Banting's dog experiments led to insulin. Radioimmunoassay (Yalow, 1977 Nobel) allowed hormone measurement.

Fix these

  • Hormones are not only sex hormones.
  • Type 2 diabetes is not just 'eating sugar'; genes, weight and activity matter.
  • Insulin is not a cure but a replacement.

India has more than 100 million people with diabetes, among the highest in the world. Indians develop it at lower body weight, linked to belly fat and genes. The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases covers diabetes screening. Iodised salt helps fight goitre. India makes much of the world's low-cost insulin.

• Hormones travel in blood to targets; slower but longer lasting.
  • Negative feedback keeps levels steady.
  • Insulin lowers, glucagon raises blood sugar.
  • Pituitary directs many glands.

Think about it:

  1. Why does a high thyroxine level reduce TSH?
  2. How do nerve and hormone signals differ in speed and duration?
